bull_bear.body: Priority on project execution and land acquisition (opportunistic). No dividend planned for FY27 as management prioritizes reinvestment for growth and maintaining debt-free status.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Raw material cost volatility (war impact); 2) Execution delays in complex redevelopment projects; 3) Regulatory approvals for pipeline projects (Paradise/Govind Dalvi); 4) High supply in suburbs making buyers 'choosy' (mitigated by amenity focus).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and optimistic; emphasizes 'safe haven' narrative for India attracting NRI capital; disciplined on debt; transparent about margin headwinds being temporary.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: War geopolitics is inadvertently boosting demand as NRIs (especially from Dubai) repatriate funds to buy 'safe' assets in India; Management cites specific instances of NRI brothers buying multiple flats for safety. Ind AS adoption was late (Q4), causing restatements but aligning future comparability.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated financial philosophy: 'Asset-light, capital-efficient business model', 'Low leverage with disciplined financial management' and 'Strong cash flows and sales momentum'.
- Reinvestment is directed rather than diversified: 'Focused reinvestment in premium housing and recurring income assets'.
- Management's forward priorities are 'accelerating project execution, selectively expanding our redevelopment portfolio, maintaining financial discipline, and delivering sustainable value for all stakeholders'.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Redevelopment-led model in Mumbai's western suburbs, where scarcity of greenfield land and regulatory reform make redevelopment a durable demand driver
- Capital-efficient, asset-light business model that management says allows it to scale efficiently
- Demonstrated execution and delivery capability — two redevelopment projects (Rashmi Vasudeo, Rashmi Celestia) delivered in FY26 alongside construction progress across four ongoing developments
- Booked pipeline of approximately 4.9 lakh sq. ft. out of a ~7.5 lakh sq. ft. portfolio, described by management as providing strong revenue visibility
- Positioning in the MMR premium/redevelopment segment, which management says commands premium valuations and attracts financially stronger buyers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory approval risk on redevelopment projects — The auditors state that redevelopment projects are exposed to risks relating to regulatory approvals, which may significantly impact the recoverability and valuation of inventory. Audit procedures included reviewing project approvals, commencement certificates and occupation certificates to assess the status of projects and potential risks impacting project completion.
- Changes in development control regulations — Explicitly named as an exposure for the Company's redevelopment projects; changes in development control regulations can alter project economics and buildable potential in Mumbai's redevelopment micro-markets.
- Contractual obligations towards society members and existing occupants — Redevelopment carries obligations towards society members / existing occupants, including rehabilitation and transit accommodation costs that form part of attributable land and development rights costs — an obligation structurally specific to the redevelopment model.
- Project execution delays — Named as an exposure of redevelopment projects; delays in the stage of physical completion affect cost to complete and the recoverability of inventory carried against long-dated projects.
- Cost escalation on long-cycle projects — Cost escalations are named as a risk; inventory valuation depends on management estimates of total projected construction and redevelopment costs to complete, so escalation directly compresses realisable margin.
- Changing market conditions affecting selling prices and demand — The determination of inventory carrying value requires management to estimate future selling prices and expected market demand; adverse movement in either would affect net realisable value.
- Estimation uncertainty in inventory valuation (Key Audit Matter) — Inventory valuation of redevelopment projects under construction and completed units held for sale was flagged as a Key Audit Matter because it involves significant management judgment and estimation uncertainty due to the long-term and complex nature of such projects, together with the materiality of the balance.
- Litigation, disputes and claims with contractors, society members and regulatory authorities — The auditors reviewed correspondence relating to material litigations, disputes and claims with contractors, society members, regulatory authorities and other stakeholders that could affect project costs or realizability.

business.body:

business.body:

These are market forecasts, not company guidance.
- [Stated sector risks] The deck itself lists watch factors: 'Foreign FDI Pullback: Foreign investment share down to 13% in Q1 2026'; 'Luxury Concentration: Luxury dominates; mid-income demand under pressure'; 'Supply Overhang Risk: 154% YoY surge in office launches'; 'Regulatory Patchwork: Uneven RERA implementation across states'.
- [Internal inconsistency - macro] The growth-driver slide cites 'GDP Resilience: 6.7% GDP and 8-9% real estate growth in 2026' while the macro slide cites '6.5- 7% GDP in 2026' and a footnote cites 'CBRE ... GDP 7.6% FY26'; the deck carries all three.
- [IR contact] Investor relations is run through Adfactors IR; company contacts named are Mahek Modi (CFO) and Saloni Nagvekar (Adfactors IR).

It is not engaged in any manufacturing activity, and management describes the model as capital-efficient and asset-light with a focus on timely project execution and handover.

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margin compression (EBITDA ~20% vs historical ~28%) due to: 1) War-driven raw material inflation impacting Rashmi Square/Signature; 2) High upfront costs for new launches (Icon/Avenue) before revenue recognition. Management expects full recovery in FY27 as these projects mature and pricing power (₹27k-28k psf) kicks in.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Accelerating in FY27 Q1 due to booking conversions; Margin: Expect bounce-back to previous levels (~27-28% EBITDA) as high-margin projects (Signature/Square) complete; Order Inflow: Strong traction in Rashmi Icon/Avenue; Capex: Minimal external funding required, self-funded via sales.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total Portfolio: 7.5L sqft; Booked: 4.92L sqft (65%); Available: 2.40L sqft. Key Projects: Rashmi Square (69% booked, 19 floors, delivery FY27), Rashmi Signature (50% booked, targeting 75%, delivery Q1 FY27), Rashmi Icon/Avenue (Early stage, high traction).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Pipeline includes Rashmi Shetal, Rashmi Gold (acquired), Rashmi Paradise, Govind Dalvi Nagar (approval stage). Potential township project outside Mumbai if clear-title land found. Geographic expansion to South Bombay/Dadar targeting ₹45k-50k psf realizations.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Redevelopment-led growth: management states that redevelopment will remain a key driver of growth in Mumbai and that the Company is well-positioned to capitalise on it with its strong execution track record and growing project pipeline.
- Disciplined asset-light strategy that management says has enabled the Company to scale efficiently while maintaining strong cash flows and operational agility.
- Geographic focus on Mumbai's western suburbs and Mumbai suburban areas, expanding the development portfolio through new project launches and redevelopment mandates.
- Maintain a debt-free balance sheet as a strong financial foundation for pursuing future growth opportunities.
- Reinvest profits rather than distribute them: the Board retained the entire FY26 profit in the business and did not recommend a dividend, believing re-investing capital in real estate business development opportunities would create more wealth and long-term value for shareholders.
- Corporate simplification via the amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary Shree Modis Navnirman Private Limited with the Company (NCLT Mumbai Bench order dated October 16th, 2025) — a strategic consolidation that management says strengthens operational capabilities, enhances efficiencies and positions the Company for scalable growth in Mumbai's redevelopment market.
- Migration from the SME Platform to the Main Board of BSE and NSE (effective 14th November 2025) to enhance market visibility, improve liquidity and reinforce the highest standards of governance and transparency.
- Structured CSR and social impact through Modis Navnirman Foundation, a Section 8 wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on January 20, 2026, enabling initiatives in education, healthcare, environmental sustainability, skill development and community welfare through a separate legal entity.
- First-time adoption of the Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) framework for the year ended March 2026, with the transition carried out from the transition date of 1 April 2024.
- Focus on near-full sell-through and negligible unsold stock — the Company cites 14 completed projects, full sell-out of Rashmi Vasudeo (Kastur Park, Borivali west) and near-full sell-out of Rashmi Celestia (L.T. Road, Borivali west).
- Sustain growth momentum supported by strong project visibility, a robust pipeline and a clear strategic roadmap, with continued commitment to timely execution and value creation.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Modi's Navnirman Limited is an asset-light real estate developer, so its expansion is measured in project footprint rather than plant capex. During FY26 the Company significantly strengthened its development pipeline with the launch of Rashmi Icon, comprising approximately 3.5 lakh sq. ft. of construction area, and the commencement of Rashmi Avenue; along with continued progress across ongoing projects, the total project portfolio expanded to around 7.5 lakh sq. ft. of construction area, of which approximately 4.9 lakh sq. ft. was already booked, providing what management describes as strong revenue visibility for the coming years. On delivery, the Company completed two redevelopment projects during the year — Rashmi Vasudeo (Kastur Park, Borivali west) and Rashmi Celestia (L.T. Road, Borivali west) — and received the Occupation Certificate for Rashmi Celestia, enabling timely handovers to customers, while maintaining strong construction progress across four ongoing developments; at year-end approximately 7.5 lakh sq. ft. of development area was under various stages of development. The Company also added to its forward pipeline by securing redevelopment mandates with an estimated Gross Development Value of approximately Rs 400 crore and above in Mumbai's western suburbs, comprising New Chitra Society, a redevelopment of 2,133 sq. mtrs situated in Kandivali west, and Bank of India Staff Sheetal, a redevelopment of 3,925 sq. mtrs situated in Borivali west. Management states it will continue to expand its redevelopment portfolio across Mumbai's high-demand western suburbs through a capital-efficient and asset-light business model, and cites 14 completed projects with negligible unsold stock. Structurally, the Company consolidated operations by amalgamating its wholly owned subsidiary Shree Modis Navnirman Private Limited with itself, and incorporated Modis Navnirman Foundation as a non-profit entity for social welfare and CSR activity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Redevelopment activity in Mumbai — supported by regulatory reforms and the scarcity of greenfield land — continues to be a powerful demand driver for developers operating in the city's densely built micro-markets.
- Indian real estate sector resilience supported by favourable demographics, increasing urbanisation and a sustained preference for home ownership.
- Premiumisation of Indian residential demand: per Knight Frank India, homes priced above Rs 1 crore accounted for 50 percent of total residential sales across the top eight cities in 2025, up from 44 percent a year earlier, with average home prices up 3-5 percent in FY26 indicating sustained pricing power among organised developers.
- Expansion of the Rs 1-2 crore mid-market bracket in Mumbai from 32 percent to 38 percent of all registrations in Q1 FY27, driven by first-time homebuyers benefiting from lower repo rates and new supply in the western suburbs.
- Monetary easing — the RBI cut the repo rate cumulatively by 100 basis points between April and December 2025 to 5.25 percent, with the MPC holding at the February 2026 review and signalling a neutral-to-accommodative stance.
- Home prices in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region are forecast to rise by approximately 5 percent, supported by constrained supply, infrastructure-driven connectivity and steady aspirational demand.
- Infrastructure catalysts — Mumbai Metro Line expansions, the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, Coastal Road and the upcoming Navi Mumbai International Airport — continue to unlock new residential and commercial micro-markets across the MMR.
- Mumbai's structural demand position: it accounted for approximately 26-28 percent of all residential sales across major Indian cities on a quarterly basis in FY26, reinforcing its status as the country's most liquid and demand-resilient housing market, with demand from HNIs, NRIs and premium end-users.
- Global decarbonisation and tightening green regulation reinforce what management calls the strategic imperative for developers like Modi's Navnirman Limited to invest in energy-efficient design, sustainable construction and green certification as a durable value creation lever, with non-compliant buildings facing meaningful risk of value erosion.
- Union Budget 2026-27 support: public capital expenditure raised to Rs 12.2 lakh crore in FY27 from Rs 11.2 lakh crore in FY26 (a 9 percent increase) is expected to unlock new real estate growth corridors, and City Economic Regions receive Rs 5,000 crore per region over five years to develop integrated urban ecosystems.
- For well-positioned urban redevelopers operating in supply-constrained markets, management says the global real estate environment — recovering real estate finance and returning institutional investors — provides a strategic tailwind.
- Total project portfolio expanded to around 7.5 lakh sq. ft. of construction area, with approximately 4.9 lakh sq. ft. already booked, which management says provides strong revenue visibility for the coming years.
- Secured redevelopment projects with an estimated Gross Development Value of approximately Rs 400 crore and above, further strengthening presence in Mumbai's western suburbs.
- New Chitra Society — a redevelopment of 2,133 sq. mtrs situated in Kandivali west.
- Bank of India Staff Sheetal — a redevelopment of 3,925 sq. mtrs situated in Borivali west.
- Rashmi Icon launched during FY26, comprising approximately 3.5 lakh sq. ft. of construction area, alongside the commencement of Rashmi Avenue.
- Four ongoing developments with strong construction progress at year-end; two redevelopment projects (Rashmi Vasudeo and Rashmi Celestia) delivered during FY26, and 14 completed projects with negligible unsold stock.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Modis Navnirman delivered record revenue (+84% YoY) and PAT (+26% YoY) in FY26 driven by project handovers (Rashmi Vasudev/Celestia) and main board migration, though margins compressed due to war-induced input costs and early-stage project expenses. The thesis hinges on converting strong NRI demand (safe-haven buying) into higher realizations (₹27k-28k psf) in FY27 to restore margins while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet.
